discovery: Precision mapping of the cosmic microwave background anisotropies with WMAP, establishing the standard cosmological model and the nearly scale-invariant, adiabatic, Gaussian primordial fluctuations

nominees.name: David N. Spergel
nominees.affiliation: Simons Foundation and Princeton University, USA

motivation: The Wilkinson Microwave Anisotropy Probe turned cosmology into a precision science. Bennett (principal investigator), Page (instrument and polarization design) and Spergel (theory and analysis lead) produced full-sky temperature and polarization maps with carefully controlled systematics. From these maps they measured the age, geometry and composition of the universe to percent-level accuracy, and they established the six-parameter LambdaCDM model as the standard description of the cosmos. WMAP showed that the primordial fluctuations are adiabatic, Gaussian and nearly scale-invariant, with a spectral index measurably below one. It detected the large-angle temperature-polarization correlation from reionization. These results made the physics of the earliest moments, including inflation, an empirical question. WMAP's statistically rigorous, open data releases set the methodological template for Planck and for every survey since. Later experiments have confirmed its results independently. This is a foundational discovery about the origin of cosmic structure.
